https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-new.text: Around 20 commercial flights across Europe received hoax bomb threats for a third consecutive day on Thursday, prompting Italian, French and Bulgarian fighter jets to scramble, flight diversions and security checks at multiple airports. All aircraft landed safely, with no explosives found.Emails sent to the Rome and Sofia airports during a series of hoax bomb alerts across Europe Thursday were signed "the fighters of the Male State", according to the text seen by AFP and the company operating Rome airport.The threats targeted several low-cost carriers, particularly flights to and from Bulgaria, Italy and the Czech Republic. Three aircraft were diverted, while at least five received military escorts after bomb alerts.Ryanair flights escorted, Aer Lingus aircraft divertedBulgaria's air force escorted three Ryanair flights heading to Sofia from Madrid, Copenhagen and London. All three aircraft underwent inspections, with no explosives discovered, an interior ministry spokesperson told AFP. Also Read: US expands online immigration filing options, touts faster processing and fraud checksFrench fighter jets accompanied an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome, forcing it to land at the Evreux military base, about 100 kilometers west of Paris.France's prime minister's office said the aircraft was escorted after its pilot allegedly failed to cooperate with authorities as expected. Evreux prosecutor Remi Coutin told AFP the pilot had allegedly refused to land at the military base, preferring a civilian airport.Aer Lingus said its airline and pilots fully cooperated with French authorities.Separately, a Ryanair flight from London to Sofia was diverted to Plovdiv, while a Wizz Air flight from Milan to Warsaw was rerouted to Vienna.Bomb threats invoke extremist groupMessages sent to Sofia airport and Rome airport operator ADR claimed explosives had been placed on multiple flights. The threats included misogynistic language and purportedly came from “fighters of the Male State”.A similar threat naming “Men's State” was reported at Birmingham Airport in Britain.The messages warned of explosions and threatened to target what they described as a feminist regime. AFP could not immediately establish any connection between the threats and Russia's Male State movement, a far-right organization designated extremist by Russian courts in 2021.Also Read: Trump renews push for permanent daylight saving time, criticizes Senate over stalled billLou Osborn, founder of Inpact, a group monitoring clandestine Russian activities, told AFP the organization uses Nazi symbolism and has thousands of members. Its links to Russian authorities remain unclear, she said.Prague Airport also received anonymous email threats, while Heathrow Airport said a threat it received was deemed not credible.Most flights land safelySeveral targeted flights reached their destinations without incident, including aircraft operated by LOT Polish Airlines, Wizz Air and Air Serbia.Four threatened planes bound for Prague also landed safely. Danish police said two flights threatened in Copenhagen arrived as scheduled, adding there had never been any danger to passengers or others at the airport.The alerts represented a small fraction of European air traffic. Eurocontrol estimated 25,072 flights were scheduled across the continent on Thursday.The latest incidents followed 10 bomb threats targeting flights on Tuesday, all of which proved to be hoaxes. Monday also saw a Wizz Air flight from London's Luton Airport to Sofia diverted to Budapest following a bomb alert.(With inputs from AFP)

Waves eroded over 20 meters of coastline in Hue. Large support frames were removed from Saigon River pedestrian bridge. And there’s more in today’s morning news round-up. Da Nang police seized this drone from a Chinese tourist who operated it illegally in a no-fly zone in the city. Photo: Da Nang Police |POLITICS -- Chairwoman of the Federation Council of the Federal Assembly of Russia Valentina Matvienko will pay an official visit to Vietnam from November 11 to 13. The visit will be made at the invitation of Vietnamese National Assembly Chairman Tran Thanh Man. -- Vietnamese Party General Secretary and State President To Lam and Prime Minister Le Minh Hung on Monday sent messages of condolence to Polish President Karol Nawrocki and Prime Minister Donald Tusk over a recent mass shooting in the city of Krakow. The November 7 shooting left many people dead and injured. |SOCIETY -- The Department of Health in Tay Ninh Province, southern Vietnam reported two cases of meningococcal disease on Monday. The first patient is a 53-year-old male factory worker, while the second is a seven-year-old schoolboy. All contacts of the patients have been traced and given preventive antibiotics. -- High waves combined with high tides have eroded a 100-meter stretch of coastline in Thuan An Ward, Hue City, central Vietnam by more than 20 meters inland, uprooting many decades-old casuarina trees. A road connecting a residential area to the beach has also been eroded, with sections of its surface peeling away and undercut gaps forming beneath it. As an immediate measure, local authorities are reviewing households living near the eroded area so they can be relocated promptly if necessary to protect lives and property. A decades-old row of casuarina trees is uprooted by waves in Hue City, central Vietnam. Photo: Nguyen Do / Tuoi Tre -- Da Nang City Police's immigration management division said on its website on Monday that it had coordinated with relevant agencies to fine a Chinese tourist VND25 million (US$980) for illegally operating a drone in a no-fly zone in the city. The tourist also had the drone confiscated. Specifically, the Chinese national was found operating a DJI Mavic 3 drone in a residential quarter in Son Tra Ward, an area designated as a no-fly zone. The operator had not obtained a flight permit from the competent authorities. Da Nang City Police advised residents, domestic and foreign tourists, and organizations and individuals wishing to use unmanned aerial vehicles or ultralight aircraft to proactively learn about and strictly comply with legal regulations, and check information on no-fly zones. -- Fourteen residents of Phu Hai fishing village in Lam Dong Province, central Vietnam have been hospitalized after eating puffer fish, with one patient in critical condition, Sai Gon Giai Phong (Liberated Saigon) newspaper reported. Binh Thuan General Hospital said on Monday morning that it was providing intensive treatment to the 14 patients for puffer fish poisoning. One of them is in extremely serious condition, having fallen into a deep coma and suffering severe kidney failure. A barge-mounted crane is used to dismantle support frames at the Saigon River pedestrian bridge construction site in Ho Chi Minh City. Photo: Ngoc Khai / Tuoi Tre -- Dozens of workers were busy dismantling large support frames at the Saigon River pedestrian bridge construction site on Monday. With the help of a crane mounted on a barge, each steel frame was carefully lowered onto the barge to ensure safety. Meanwhile, other groups of workers continued construction at both ends of the bridge, near Bach Dang Wharf and Thu Thiem. Construction teams are focusing on completing the bridge deck, installing railings and an artistic lighting system, and landscaping the areas at both ends of the bridge. The bridge is scheduled to open to traffic before the 2027 Lunar New Year. Gong Festival in Central Highlands A gong performance at the 2026 Gia Lai Gong Festival in Vietnam's Central Highlands.
